Identify whether the current protocol satisfies the contract; apply the smallest justified correction or preserve it if adequate. Work only in this supplied fixture, keep Java17 without preview or new dependencies, and distinguish local callback checks from integration with a physical device. Do not infer correctness or a defect from class names alone.
taskInputs.contract:
# Capture protocol

App owns the driver, completion-delivery object and view for its lifetime. All calls in this
fixture run on one application thread; there is no concurrent request thread or background I/O.
The selected delivery implementation is part of this deployment's supported contract.

A first request starts one capture. If the driver reports captured, the view is updated once
and the coordinator must remain DONE after the call stack and pending delivery have finished.
Further requests in RUNNING, DONE or UNKNOWN do not start another capture.

The driver can also throw without a terminal outcome. The protocol then records UNKNOWN and
preserves that outcome; the caller receives the original failure. Automatic retry is not allowed.
The fixture does not promise cancellation, restart recovery, multiple operation generations or
physical-device idempotency. Driver/view ownership is unchanged by the review.

# Capture feature fixture

Compile target Java17; no preview or dependencies.
Compile sources with javac --release 17 -d out src/*.java.
The source includes a small local driver/view boundary and two completion-delivery implementations.
Read Assembly.java to determine which delivery this deployment selects.

The manual delivery drain exists for deterministic local execution. These sources are not a
physical driver integration and contain no external side effects. Only one capture is admitted.

expected: Trace Assembly selecting Inline, Driver.capture reporting synchronously, and the callback's DONE write being overwritten by request's later RUNNING write.
Demonstrate final phase mismatch after callback completion; one application thread does not eliminate reentrancy.
Use a minimal state/effect ordering correction (record RUNNING before invoking the participant), or preserve another justified serialization policy with the actual caller/delivery contract explained.
Preserve DONE duplicate-admission behavior and UNKNOWN/no-blind-retry behavior on failure; test normal and failure paths.
Retain the small coordinator/ports unless actual separate protocol responsibility warrants a split; do not add a command bus merely to route this interaction.
failureConditions: Assumes Executor.execute is asynchronous or calls this a data race requiring ConcurrentHashMap.
Drops the required nested completion with a guard, or leaves DONE overwritten.
Introduces mandatory bus/framework, unsafe repeated capture after failure, version/dependency upgrade, or claims physical-device integration.

expected: Trace Assembly selecting Queued and drain occurring after request; preserve adequate sequencing under this supported delivery contract.
Check RUNNING before drain and DONE after drain, with a single capture/view update and no duplicate request effect.
Do not force a bus or label the current flow broken solely because the unused Inline implementation would expose a different contract.
May propose making the state/effect boundary robust to future inline delivery as optional hardening, explicitly distinguishing it from a current reproduced defect.
Preserve UNKNOWN/no-blind-retry and Java17 baseline; no claim of transaction or device integration.
